prerequisites: Good knowledge of elementary mathematics (algebra, geometry and trigonometry)
Fundamental notions of differential and integral calculus

learning_outcomes.text: Provide a basic understanding of the foundations of Classical Mechanics.
Develop the ability to reason scientifically and apply abstract mathematical models and concepts to real and concrete scientific problems.
Acquire a conscious operational ability in solving simple numerical exercises.
Learn the basics of the scientific method, common to all experimental disciplines.
Learn a significant selection of Classical Mechanics topics, also presented through everyday life experiences or applications to the medical engineering sector.
Identify the physical laws that govern the phenomena involved.
Arrive at the definition of adequate solution strategies.
Be equipped with useful schemes to be able to independently express evaluations on problems of reasonable complexity.
Be able to use correct terminology and technical-scientific language appropriate to the treatment of the topics learned.
Be able to independently deepen the skills acquired and use tools for the continuous updating of their knowledge.

syllabus_topics: Physical quantities and units of measurement
Fluid mechanics: hydrostatics and fluid dynamics
assessment_rules: The exam consists of a written test followed by an oral test. The written test (duration 2 hours) consists of the resolution of three problems of Mechanics. Students who pass the written test (minimum threshold to reach 18/30) will be admitted to take the subsequent oral test. The oral test consists of the illustration of some of the main topics covered in the program, starting from a discussion of the previous written test. The final evaluation will be expressed in thirtieths.
